summary: The main article describes a dual palladium/photoredox catalytic system for the ortho-acylation of acetophenone oxime ethers. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope schemes for both benzoylformic acids and oxime ethers, and mechanistic studies including radical trapping and ESR analysis.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Drugs containing benzophenone structure.
items.description: Displays chemical structures of biologically active molecules like ketoprofen and fenofibrate that contain the benzophenone scaffold.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Decarboxylative cross-coupling reactions in the literature and this work. FG: functional group.
items.description: Comparison of previous decarboxylative cross-coupling methods with the current photocatalytic C-H activation approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions.
items.description: Screening of palladium catalysts, photocatalysts, and solvents to determine the optimal conditions for the ortho-benzoylation of acetophenone oxime ether.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Scope of benzoylformic acid.
items.description: Exploration of various substituted benzoylformic acids in the decarboxylative acylation reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Scope of acetophenone oxime ether.
items.description: Investigation of the substrate scope for different acetophenone oxime ethers, including cyclic and drug-derived variants.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Gram-scale reaction and further transformation.
items.description: Demonstration of the reaction on a larger scale and subsequent synthetic transformations of the products into phthalazines and other derivatives.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Preliminary mechanistic study.
items.description: Control experiments including radical trapping with TEMPO and kinetic isotope effect (KIE) studies.

items.heading: Scheme 6
items.caption: Plausible reaction mechanism.
items.description: Proposed catalytic cycle involving photoredox-mediated radical generation and palladium-catalyzed C-H activation.
